sources.README.md:
# Draft workspace

The workspace lets a user open documents, edit their text, and move between
documents. It renders the active document together with an outline, a save badge,
and breadcrumb history. Saved document data remains available after navigation,
and workspace integrations may react to successful saves.

`select(id)`, `edit(text)`, and `close()` are the public navigation and editing
operations. The outline and breadcrumbs should continue to describe what the user
is viewing, while the store should retain accepted edits. Existing integrations
and ordinary navigation behavior must keep working when draft writes are
coalesced.

The shared trailing-task utility is also used by search preview. Preview is a
transient feature with its own hide behavior and is outside the requested draft
save change.

This fixture uses normal JavaScript modules and an injected timer adapter. No
framework lifecycle is simulated.

public_inputs.task:
# Coalesce draft saves in the workspace

The editor currently writes to the workspace store on every edit. Change editor
autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save
only its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate.
Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior. Keep
search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task.

limitations: This guidance applies when deferred work invokes a synchronous notifying store; it does not define behavior for asynchronous persistence, timer-adapter failures, store-write exceptions, or exceptions thrown by subscribers.
The 120 ms delay and document/visit identities are task-specific parameters; other applications must derive their delay and ownership identity from their own public requirements.
The sources support flushing accepted draft work at navigation and disposal boundaries, but do not require one particular internal token or generation-counter implementation.
Acceptance attempt 1 and public syntax checks support this pattern for the supplied workspace, but one passing attempt does not establish cross-task causality.

rules.body: Apply this pattern when edits must be trailing-edge coalesced while accepted pending data must survive navigation or disposal, and persistence synchronously notifies integrations. TASK requires: "after 120 ms without another edit, save only its latest text" and "Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior."

Bind each deferred batch to the document and committed visit that accepted the edit. Each later edit in that batch replaces the retained text and restarts the quiet interval; never retarget pending text to the document selected later.

Use the existing trailing-task semantics documented in src/trailing-task.js: "cancel discards work; flush runs it now" and "Retire the old batch before invoking work, which can enqueue another batch." Thus clear the old batch before store.write so a synchronous callback can establish an independent new batch.

At select, close, or disposal, first retire the departing document's save-status subscription, then flush its accepted pending draft. This preserves data while satisfying src/save-status.js: "A close/open request retires the departing badge immediately: it must produce no further output, including during that navigation call."

Treat synchronous store notification as a reentrancy barrier. After boundary flushing or any other store.write returns, verify that the initiating navigation request is still current before rendering, committing a visit, or clearing the projection. A newer select or close invoked by onSaved takes precedence over the suspended outer operation.

Assign a distinct monotonically increasing identity to every requested visit, including consecutive requests for the same document ID, and commit the projection only if the editor retained that exact request. Preserve src/navigation-projection.js's rule that "A committed visit is distinct even when its document id matches the previous one."

Do not emit a store write for every edit, save superseded text, discard accepted pending draft work at a persistence boundary, allow a retired badge to render during boundary flushing, or let an older navigation continuation overwrite a synchronously reentrant request.

Do not alter the independent search-preview task. TASK says: "Keep search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task." Its existing 40 ms delay and hide-time cancellation remain separate from draft persistence.

Verify at least: multiple edits yield one latest-text write after 120 ms; select, close, and dispose preserve pending text; the departing badge is detached before a boundary write; onSaved can synchronously select or close without an older operation overwriting editor/projection state; reentrant edits form a new batch; repeated same-ID visits remain distinct; and search preview retains its 40 ms and hide behavior.

checkpoints: After any synchronous store.write callback returns, re-check whether the editor/navigation operation that initiated the write is still current before committing further editor or projection state.
At a select, close, or dispose boundary, preserve the latest accepted edit for the departing document while retiring its save-status subscription before that write can notify subscribers.
Before committing a requested visit to the navigation projection, verify that synchronous save integrations have not replaced or closed that request.
When a trailing batch fires or is flushed, retire that batch before invoking store.write so reentrant edits can create a distinct new batch.
forbidden_effects: Do not write every edit directly to the store.
Do not save superseded text from an earlier edit in the same burst.
Do not discard an accepted pending draft merely because the user selects another document, closes the editor, or disposes the workspace.
Do not allow a departing document's save badge to render during or after the navigation call that retires it.
Do not let an outer select/open/close operation overwrite a newer navigation request made synchronously by onSaved.
Do not coalesce distinct committed visits merely because their document IDs match.
Do not change search-preview timing, cancellation, or hide behavior.
Do not modify the draft store's synchronous write and inline-notification semantics.
lifecycle_identity: A pending autosave belongs to the document and committed visit that accepted the edit; later navigation must not retarget that text to the newly selected document.
Each requested visit has its own monotonically assigned visit identity, including consecutive visits to the same document ID.
A mounted save-status subscription belongs to one open document and is retired immediately by close/open navigation.
The trailing batch must be cleared before its work callback runs, allowing a reentrant edit to establish a new batch without being erased by completion of the old one.

obligations.text: Coalesce a burst of editor edits and write only the latest text after 120 ms with no subsequent edit.
Use the existing trailing-task behavior where appropriate, including its latest-arguments batching and reentrancy-safe retirement of the old batch before work runs.
Preserve accepted pending edits across select, close, and workspace disposal boundaries so navigation does not lose draft persistence; boundary handling may flush the departing batch immediately.
Keep document rendering, selection, outline, and breadcrumb projection consistent with the navigation request that remains current after any synchronous save callbacks finish.
Retire the departing document's save-status subscription before a navigation-boundary save can notify listeners, while allowing workspace-level onSaved integrations to observe successful saves.

Account for synchronous reentrancy from store notifications: if onSaved selects, closes, or otherwise changes navigation during a save, the newer request takes precedence over the suspended outer operation.
Leave search preview behavior and its 40 ms timing unchanged.

ordering_barriers: For ordinary editing, each new edit cancels/replaces the prior scheduled batch and restarts the 120 ms quiet interval.
The store write occurs only for the latest arguments retained by the batch.
At navigation retirement, detach the old save-status listener before persisting its pending draft, because store notifications execute inline.
A navigation request must not commit its projection until any departing-draft persistence and its synchronous integration callbacks have returned and the request is confirmed still current.
The old trailing batch is cleared before store.write invokes external callbacks; edits initiated by those callbacks form a new pending batch.
Projection commit follows successful retention of the corresponding editor visit; projection clear follows a close that remains current.
preservation: select(id), edit(text), and close() remain the public navigation/editing operations.
Opening a retained visit renders that document using store.read(id).
Closing clears the active editor rendering and navigation selection; disposal still detaches the workspace store subscription and clears editor/projection state.
The outline and breadcrumb trail continue to describe the visit the user is viewing, and each committed visit remains distinct even for repeated document IDs.
Draft-store writes remain synchronous, increment revisions, update the record before notification, and notify currently subscribed listeners inline.
Workspace integrations continue receiving successful-save events and the navigation object.
Saved document data remains available after navigation, including edits accepted shortly before navigation.
Search preview continues using its independent 40 ms trailing task, and hide continues discarding its pending query.
scope: Change draft editor autosave behavior and the workspace coordination needed to preserve navigation, persistence, save-status retirement, and synchronous-integration behavior.
Reuse src/trailing-task.js for draft-save coalescing where appropriate.
Do not change the independent search-preview feature.
